question: Does active-step reference disclosure reduce observed reference reads and execution overhead without losing required workflow behavior?

arms.A: Same canonical router and available documents, plus experiment-only eager document-read timing instruction.
arms.B: Same canonical router and available documents, current active-step-only disclosure/read timing.

order: Repeat 1 AB; repeat 2 BA within each model/workload block; alternating model blocks. Provider cache residency is uncontrolled.
budget_note: Subscription login, no new API keys. Caps checked at emitted usage events; telemetry can arrive only at episode end. No actual-billing assertion. Stop on inaccessible model, absent router attribution or invalid grader before expanding trials.
useful_effect: At least 10% lower paired price-weighted input cost or reference-read content tokens, with no observed critical correctness/semantic regression; workload-specific screening only.
quality: External acceptance checks plus attributed router/read/workflow evidence. Two repeats cannot establish a <=2 pp non-inferiority bound.
exclusions: Infrastructure failures retained and marked inconclusive. Agent errors, valid budget exhaustion and incomplete work count as failures. No outcome-selected reruns.
closure: Pilot only. Does not satisfy issue290 >=5 paired repeats per family; no automatic closure or general benefit claim.
public_selection_provenance: 0b221bf75b89b5834bc72869ddb9a6847db9760d; source selection reused, not the unrelated skill-text vs vanilla contrast.
required_preflight: normal Node require and fixture commands work
reporting: Per model/host and workload: completion, actual reference reads, uncached/cache creation/cache read/input/output/reasoning where exposed, estimated cost only where priced, wall time, tool counts, all errors/exclusions. Missing fields are unknown.
